328.text:
A generation ago, many families bought the same brand of soap, car or bank for decades, and some argue that brand loyalty is declining. I agree to a large extent, since shoppers compare prices and reviews easily, although strong brands still keep devoted customers.

To begin with, brand loyalty is declining in many categories because switching is easy. Online comparison, store brands and endless choice make changing simple. A shopper who sees on her phone that another brand of washing powder is cheaper and has better reviews, for example, can change within seconds, and a promotion can persuade her to try something new. Supermarkets sell their own labels that look similar to famous brands but cost less, and young consumers in particular are more willing to try new products recommended by friends or influencers. Subscriptions and apps allow customers to move from one service to another with a few taps, and economic uncertainty makes many people more careful with money.

However, strong brands with identity and loyalty programmes keep devoted customers. Some people remain committed to certain makers of phones, sports shoes or cars because the brand expresses who they are, and they accept higher prices. A person who has used the same smartphone system for ten years, for example, may stay with it because his photographs, apps and friends are connected to it. Airlines and shops use points and discounts to reward repeat purchases. Brands must earn loyalty through quality and service. Companies that treat customers well, respond quickly to complaints and keep improving their products are more likely to be trusted, and trust is more durable than a lower price.

In conclusion, I agree to a large extent that brand loyalty is declining, but companies with excellent products and a clear identity can still retain it.

Thương hiệu mạnh bản sắc, chương trình thành viên giữ khách: một số trung thành điện thoại, giày, xe vì thể hiện bản thân, chấp nhận giá cao; ví dụ người dùng cùng hệ điện thoại 10 năm vì ảnh, ứng dụng, bạn kết nối; hãng bay, cửa hàng điểm, giảm giá; phải giành lòng trung thành: chất lượng, dịch vụ, xử lý khiếu nại, tin cậy bền hơn giá thấp.
Largely agree; công ty xuất sắc vẫn giữ được.

330.text:
Some online retailers now promise to deliver goods within hours of an order, and this essay will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of same-day delivery for consumers before explaining my own view.

On the positive side, same-day delivery is convenient for urgent needs. Customers get goods in hours and can shop online for emergencies. A person whose washing machine breaks down on a Monday morning, for example, can order a part and have it fitted by the evening, and a parent who forgets a birthday present can still please a child on the same day. It saves travel time, particularly for people who are ill, elderly or without a car, and it allows busy workers to shop in the evening. Competition between companies has made the service cheaper than in the past, and some customers enjoy being able to track the courier on a map.

On the negative side, extra fees, fragmented trips, pollution and pressure on couriers make it less attractive in the long term. Many same-day services charge a premium for speed, which means that people pay more for goods that they could have waited for. Vans that make many small deliveries produce more emissions than a single large weekly delivery, and packaging often increases. Couriers who must meet tight deadlines may work long hours for low pay and take risks in traffic. Easy ordering also encourages impulse purchases and returns. Same-day delivery should be reserved for genuinely urgent purchases. Consumers can use standard delivery for ordinary items, group their orders and choose delivery options that are slower but cheaper and more environmentally friendly.

In conclusion, same-day delivery offers real convenience, but its costs for workers and the environment are significant. On balance, I believe that it is useful only in urgent situations.

plan.think: Mở bài nêu nhà bán lẻ hứa giao trong vài giờ.

Tiện cho nhu cầu khẩn cấp: nhận hàng trong vài giờ; ví dụ máy giặt hỏng sáng thứ Hai đặt linh kiện, lắp tối, phụ huynh quên quà sinh nhật vẫn làm con vui; tiết kiệm thời gian cho người ốm, già, không xe; người bận mua tối; cạnh tranh rẻ hơn; theo dõi shipper trên bản đồ.

Phí, chuyến lẻ, ô nhiễm, áp lực người giao làm kém hấp dẫn dài hạn: phí cao cho tốc độ; xe giao nhiều đơn nhỏ thải nhiều hơn một đơn lớn hàng tuần, bao bì; shipper hạn chót chặt làm nhiều giờ lương thấp, rủi ro giao thông; dễ đặt gây mua bốc đồng, trả hàng; dành cho đơn khẩn cấp; giao tiêu chuẩn, gộp đơn, lựa chọn chậm rẻ hơn, thân thiện môi trường.
Chỉ hữu ích trong tình huống khẩn cấp.

337.text:
After earthquakes, famines and wars, rich countries send money, food and experts to poorer ones, and some believe that international aid helps development. I agree to a large extent, since aid can save lives and build services, although its success depends on how it is used.

To begin with, international aid helps development when it is targeted, transparent and builds local capacity. It saves lives in emergencies and funds clinics, schools and infrastructure. A vaccination programme financed from abroad, for example, can protect millions of children from diseases that poor governments cannot afford to fight, and a grant for rural roads or clean water allows farmers to sell their crops and families to stay healthy. Aid has contributed to major improvements in child survival and school enrolment over recent decades. Technical assistance also trains local teachers, doctors and engineers, who then continue the work without outside help.

However, corruption, dependency and poorly designed projects can waste money. If officials steal funds, or if donors give food that destroys local farmers' markets, aid may do more harm than good. Countries that receive aid for many years may stop building their own tax systems and rely on outside decisions. Some projects are chosen by donors without asking communities, and they fail when equipment breaks and no one can repair it. Aid should therefore support local ownership. Funds should be monitored and published, projects should be designed with the people who will use them, and money should go to areas such as health, education and infrastructure that create lasting benefits. Trade fairness and debt relief are also essential if poor countries are to grow.

In conclusion, I agree that international aid helps development to a large extent, provided that it is well targeted, transparent and designed with local people.

Giúp khi có mục tiêu, minh bạch, xây năng lực địa phương: cứu mạng khẩn cấp, tài trợ trạm y tế, trường, hạ tầng; ví dụ chương trình tiêm chủng tài trợ nước ngoài bảo vệ hàng triệu trẻ khỏi bệnh chính phủ nghèo không lo nổi; khoản cho đường nông thôn, nước sạch giúp bán nông sản, khoẻ; viện trợ góp cải thiện sống sót trẻ, đi học; hỗ trợ kỹ thuật đào tạo giáo viên, bác sĩ, kỹ sư địa phương.

Tham nhũng, phụ thuộc, dự án thiết kế kém lãng phí: quan chức biển thủ, thực phẩm phá chợ nông dân địa phương; nước nhận lâu ngừng xây hệ thống thuế; dự án do nhà tài trợ chọn không hỏi cộng đồng thất bại khi máy hỏng; hỗ trợ sở hữu địa phương: theo dõi, công bố, thiết kế cùng người dùng, đầu tư y tế, giáo dục, hạ tầng; công bằng thương mại, xoá nợ.
Đồng ý nếu nhắm đúng, minh bạch, thiết kế cùng dân địa phương.

341.text:
Many countries have signed agreements that remove tariffs and quotas, and the question is whether the advantages of free trade outweigh the disadvantages. This essay will discuss both sides before explaining my own view.

On the positive side, free trade raises efficiency and consumer choice. Removing tariffs lowers prices and widens markets. A family in a small country that can buy cars from Japan, wine from France and clothing from Vietnam, for example, enjoys far more variety at lower prices than it could if only domestic producers were protected. Exporters can sell to millions of customers abroad, which allows them to grow, to hire more workers and to invest in better technology. Competition forces firms to improve quality and to cut waste, and specialisation lets each country concentrate on what it does best. Many economists believe that open trade has increased global income and lifted millions of people out of poverty.

On the negative side, free trade damages uncompetitive sectors. Domestic industries and workers who cannot compete may collapse, and standards can be undercut. A farming region that faces cheap imported grain, for example, may lose many farms, and the communities that depend on them decline. Countries can become dependent on imported food or medicines, which is dangerous in a crisis. Companies may also move production to places with weak environmental or labour laws. Gains outweigh losses only with adjustment support. Governments should provide retraining, regional investment and temporary assistance for those who lose their jobs, and they should include labour and environmental standards in trade agreements.

In conclusion, free trade brings large benefits in efficiency and choice. On balance, I believe that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, provided that governments protect those who are harmed by it.

Hiệu quả, lựa chọn: bỏ thuế giảm giá, mở thị trường; ví dụ gia đình nước nhỏ mua xe Nhật, rượu Pháp, quần áo Việt Nam đa dạng, giá thấp hơn chỉ bảo hộ sản xuất trong nước; nhà xuất khẩu bán cho hàng triệu khách nước ngoài, thuê thêm, đầu tư công nghệ; cạnh tranh nâng chất lượng, giảm lãng phí; chuyên môn hoá; thu nhập toàn cầu tăng, thoát nghèo.

Hại ngành kém cạnh tranh: ngành nội địa, công nhân sụp đổ, tiêu chuẩn bị hạ; ví dụ vùng nông nghiệp đối mặt gạo, ngũ cốc nhập giá rẻ mất nhiều trang trại, cộng đồng suy; phụ thuộc nhập khẩu thực phẩm, thuốc nguy hiểm khi khủng hoảng; công ty chuyển đến nơi luật lỏng; hỗ trợ chuyển đổi: đào tạo lại, đầu tư vùng, trợ cấp tạm thời, tiêu chuẩn lao động, môi trường trong hiệp định.
Ưu hơn nhược nếu bảo vệ người bị hại.

390.text:
Several countries have tested the idea of giving every adult a regular payment, whatever their income, and this essay will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of universal basic income before explaining my own view.

On the positive side, universal basic income reduces poverty and insecurity. A guaranteed payment gives everyone a floor, lets people retrain or care for family and replaces complex benefits. A woman who loses her job, for example, can pay for rent and food while she studies for a new career, without waiting for officials to assess her case. Because the money is paid to everyone, there is no stigma and no complicated test, which reduces administration costs and the number of people who fail to claim support. Experiments in Finland and Kenya suggest that recipients often experience less stress and better health. As automation removes some jobs, a basic income could protect people from sudden unemployment and encourage entrepreneurship, since failure is less frightening.

On the negative side, universal basic income is very costly and may weaken work incentives. Paying everyone needs high taxes or cuts in other services, and some of the money goes to people who do not need it. Critics fear that some recipients will work less, though research so far shows small effects. A payment that is too low will not end poverty, while one that is generous may cause inflation, since prices adjust to extra spending power. Pilot schemes should test the effects first. Governments can start with targeted groups or regions, measure the results on jobs, health and spending and then decide whether to expand.

In conclusion, basic income has attractive benefits but serious costs. On balance, I believe that its advantages justify careful testing, although a full national scheme should only follow convincing evidence.

392.text:
Defective toys, contaminated food and faulty electrical goods cause injuries every year, and some argue that stricter consumer protection laws improve safety. I agree to a large extent, since standards and penalties make firms avoid dangerous products, although enforcement matters as much as the laws themselves.

To begin with, stricter consumer protection laws improve safety by setting standards and punishing negligence. Mandatory testing, recalls and heavy fines force firms to avoid dangerous products. A toy manufacturer that must prove its products are free of poisonous paint before selling them, for example, will check its suppliers carefully, since a failure could lead to a ban and a costly lawsuit. Clear labelling of ingredients, allergens and warnings helps buyers to make safe choices, and rules on cooling and hygiene in food production reduce poisoning. Countries with strong consumer agencies, such as those in northern Europe, have lower rates of accidents from household products. When dangerous goods are found, laws allow quick recalls that protect others.

However, compliance costs and weak enforcement can reduce the benefit. Small companies may find the paperwork and testing expensive, which can raise prices or reduce the variety of products, and rules that are not checked are ignored. Online marketplaces make it easy to import cheap goods that avoid inspection. Strong laws with effective inspection protect the public. Governments should fund inspectors and laboratories, hold online platforms responsible for unsafe items sold through them, and cooperate internationally to track dangerous products. Consumers can also help by reporting problems and by reading labels carefully.

In conclusion, I agree to a large extent that stricter consumer protection laws improve safety, provided that they are enforced and designed with small businesses in mind.

395.text:
Bitcoin and other digital currencies have grown from a niche idea into assets worth trillions, and the question is how far they will affect global finance within twenty years. I believe that they will change payments and settlement considerably, although they will not replace traditional money.

To begin with, digital currencies will change payments. They can make cross-border transfers cheap and widen access to finance. A migrant worker who sends money to her family, for example, may pay a small fee and see it arrive within minutes, instead of paying high commissions and waiting for days. Millions of people in countries with weak banking systems already use mobile money, and digital wallets allow them to save, borrow and trade without a bank account. Many central banks are developing their own digital currencies, which would allow instant, low-cost payments between businesses and individuals and give governments better information about the economy. Smart contracts could automate settlement in securities and trade finance.

However, price swings, fraud and the risk to monetary control mean central banks are cautious. The value of some cryptocurrencies has fallen by half in weeks, which makes them unreliable for everyday use, and scams and thefts from exchanges have cost investors billions. If large amounts of money moved outside the banking system, authorities would find it harder to manage interest rates and to stop money laundering. State-backed digital money is more likely than private coins to dominate. Governments will probably regulate private coins strictly, require exchanges to follow banking rules and issue their own digital currencies to keep control of the monetary system.

In conclusion, digital currencies will affect global finance to a considerable extent over the next twenty years, mainly through faster payments and official digital money, but they are unlikely to replace existing currencies.

410.text:
Water, electricity, gas and public transport networks were once run by governments in many countries, but several have sold them to private companies, and this essay will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of privatising utilities before explaining my own view.

On the positive side, privatisation can bring investment and efficiency. Private owners may raise capital from investors, introduce modern technology and reduce waste. A privatised power company that installs smart meters and repairs its network, for example, may cut losses and improve the quality of supply. The government saves money that it would have used for investment, and it can spend it on schools or hospitals instead. Competition between suppliers of electricity or gas can offer customers lower prices and better service, and private managers are free from political interference in decisions such as hiring and pricing.

On the negative side, utilities are natural monopolies, so privatisation risks higher prices and neglect. Water, power and gas networks cannot be duplicated, so customers cannot switch, and private owners may raise bills and underinvest while paying dividends. A water company that pays large dividends but leaves old pipes leaking, for example, harms both customers and the environment. Poor households may struggle to pay rising bills for essential services, and unprofitable rural areas may receive worse service. Where privatisation has been poorly regulated, the results have been disappointing. Public ownership or strict regulation protects consumers. If utilities are privatised, an independent regulator must set price limits, require investment, publish performance data and punish failure, and the government should be ready to take control if a company collapses.

In conclusion, privatising utilities can provide capital and efficiency, but it creates serious risks. On balance, I believe that the disadvantages outweigh the advantages for essential networks.

418.text:
In villages and city slums, a small loan can mean the difference between a stall that stays closed and one that supports a family, and this essay will discuss how microfinance impacts small entrepreneurs, focusing on access to capital and on the risks of debt.

To begin with, microfinance can help small entrepreneurs start and grow businesses. Tiny loans let poor people buy stock or tools and earn income, especially women. A woman who borrows the equivalent of fifty dollars to buy a sewing machine, for example, can make clothes to sell, repay the loan from her profits and then borrow again to expand. Traditional banks usually refuse such customers because they have no property and the loans are too small to be profitable. Microfinance institutions use group lending and community pressure instead of collateral, and many provide training and savings accounts. Studies have found that access to credit increases household income, improves food and schooling and gives women more influence at home.

However, high interest and debt traps limit the benefits. Because administration is costly, rates can be very high, and borrowers who cannot repay may take new loans to pay old ones, falling deeper into debt. Pressure from group members or collectors can cause stress and, in extreme cases, tragedy. Not every borrower is a natural entrepreneur, and many use loans for consumption instead of investing. Training and regulation make it work. Lenders should offer business advice, set fair interest rates and avoid abusive collection, and governments should supervise the sector and promote savings and insurance products alongside credit.

In conclusion, microfinance can empower small entrepreneurs by giving them capital, but it needs responsible lending to prevent debt problems.

421.text:
In some countries, shops, buses and even street vendors no longer accept banknotes, and the question is whether the advantages of a cashless economy outweigh privacy concerns. This essay will discuss both sides before explaining my own view.

On the positive side, a cashless economy is efficient and harder to abuse. Payments are fast and transactions can be tracked, which reduces crime. A trader who accepts only electronic payments, for example, no longer has to guard a till full of notes or visit the bank each evening, and customers can pay with a touch. Because every payment leaves a record, tax evasion, bribery and money laundering become more difficult, and governments collect more revenue. Printing, transporting and counting cash is expensive, so a digital system saves money. Digital payments also make online business and international trade easier and provide data that help banks to offer credit to people with no collateral.

On the negative side, privacy concerns and exclusion are serious. Every purchase becomes visible to banks and, potentially, to governments and advertisers. A person who buys medicine or donates to a political cause, for example, may not want that information to be stored and analysed. Data leaks and hacking could expose millions of customers, and a system failure can leave citizens unable to buy food. Elderly people, the poor and visitors may lack access to digital payments. Cash should remain an option, and laws should protect personal data by limiting what banks and companies may record and share, giving customers control over its use and punishing misuse severely. Offering anonymous low-value digital payments could also reduce the risk.

In conclusion, a cashless economy offers efficiency and security against crime, but it raises real privacy problems. On balance, I believe that the benefits outweigh the concerns only if strong data protection and cash alternatives are guaranteed.

Hiệu quả, khó lạm dụng: thanh toán nhanh, theo dõi giảm tội phạm; ví dụ người bán chỉ nhận điện tử không giữ quầy tiền mặt, không ra ngân hàng mỗi tối, khách chạm; ghi lại khó trốn thuế, hối lộ, rửa tiền, chính phủ thu nhiều; in, vận chuyển, đếm tiền tốn kém; mua online, thương mại quốc tế; dữ liệu giúp ngân hàng cho vay.

422.text:
In many cities, ordinary workers cannot afford to buy or rent near their jobs, and the question is to what extent governments should intervene in housing markets to control prices. I believe that governments should intervene to a considerable extent, but they should favour measures that increase supply over rigid price controls.

To begin with, markets alone leave many people priced out, so some intervention is justified. Housing is a basic need, and when prices rise faster than wages, families are forced to spend a large share of their income on rent or leave the city. Social housing, planning reform and taxes on speculation help. A city that builds thousands of affordable flats on public land, for example, offers low-income families a secure home and also reduces pressure on private rents. Governments can simplify planning rules so that more homes are built, tax empty properties and second homes, and give housing allowances to those with the lowest incomes. Without such action, housing may become a privilege for the wealthy.

However, rigid rent caps can discourage building. If the law holds rents below market levels, landlords may stop maintaining properties or sell them, and developers may build fewer homes, which makes shortages worse. Price controls also benefit the people who already have a flat, not those who are searching. Targeted intervention keeps homes affordable. The best approach combines increased supply, which brings prices down over time, with temporary protection for tenants against sudden large rises, and support for those who cannot afford even moderate rents. Governments should also monitor the market and adjust policy when conditions change, since housing problems differ between cities.

In conclusion, governments should intervene in housing markets to a considerable extent, mainly by increasing supply and protecting vulnerable households, rather than by imposing strict price controls.

analysis.type_vi: Extent: chính phủ can thiệp thị trường nhà ở để kiểm soát giá đến đâu

plan.think: Mở bài nêu công nhân thường không mua, thuê nổi gần nơi làm; đáp: can thiệp đáng kể nhưng ưu tiên tăng cung hơn kiểm soát giá cứng.

Thị trường một mình để nhiều người không đủ khả năng: nhà là nhu cầu cơ bản, giá tăng nhanh hơn lương; nhà xã hội, cải cách quy hoạch, thuế đầu cơ; ví dụ thành phố xây hàng nghìn căn giá phải chăng trên đất công cho gia đình thu nhập thấp nhà an toàn, giảm áp lực giá thuê tư; đơn giản quy hoạch, đánh thuế nhà trống, nhà thứ hai, trợ cấp nhà ở; nếu không nhà là đặc quyền người giàu.

Trần giá thuê cứng có thể nản xây: chủ nhà ngừng bảo trì, bán; nhà phát triển xây ít, thiếu hụt nặng; kiểm soát giá lợi người đã có nhà không phải người tìm; nhắm mục tiêu: tăng cung giảm giá dần, bảo vệ tạm tăng đột ngột, hỗ trợ người không trả nổi; giám sát, điều chỉnh vì mỗi thành phố khác.
Can thiệp đáng kể chủ yếu tăng cung, bảo vệ hộ dễ tổn thương, không kiểm soát giá cứng.
